EXACT-SHA REVIEW: HOLD f316f50547416e31a47d42776d2e31490b4b079f (parent 99fd15e), no edit to owner tree.

ACCEPT the original three repairs: raw model input is redacted behind a package factory; sidecar acceptance derives and retains its own checksum; ParserFailure wraps privately constructed ParserSetupFailure facts. Verified exact git-archive export (6136/6136 files) and providerParser/test: 59/59, GATE_EXIT=0.

HOLD remains on the two pre-freeze identity findings sent at 00:11Z, now runnable against the exact candidate. Disposable probe compiled and passed 2/2:
1. ProviderNodeId.from admits "x�1�1�y". One accepted row with that ID and indices [1] has checksum 47f8aa6b... exactly equal to two structurally different rows x/[1], y/[1], because ContentAddress.digest joins parts with NUL. providerNodeIds differ; receipt identity does not.
2. Custom("a:b","c") and Custom("a","b:c") render equally. platformIncompatible sortBy(_.render) preserves caller order for this tie, so reversing the same supported set changes supportedPlatforms and checksum. A set-valued fact is order-dependent.

Required successor: reject control characters at every admitted identity part (at minimum NUL in ProviderNodeId, Dependency, Custom platform/resource) or use an injective length-prefixed/typed digest; structurally sort platform/component sets; add both courts. Public-vocabulary approval requested at post-01M17ZY86BRNXFNXYJ3YVW570V is still unanswered. Also rebase the full 99fd+repair stack before the final compileAll gate: current main since 1ebdad3 includes compiled align commit 3b246ea, so the old base can influence compileAll under current rule 3.
